mission: Find U.S. communities, farm systems and essential-service corridors whose resilience is unusually dependent on diesel trucking because rail, navigable water, local production, income or redundancy are weak; identify practical substitutions and bounded places that deserve child investigations.

include: rural and remote towns far from rail and navigable water
short-line rail connections and transload opportunities
tribal, frontier, island and remote community logistics where public evidence exists
pickup/van/light-truck substitution for smaller critical loads
local food, water, compost, manure, repair and reciprocal-load networks
farm financial stress and ownership/tenure change
exclude: assuming national averages describe a town
inferring protected traits from names or geography

questions: Which places have no cheap bulk-mode substitute when trucking becomes unaffordable?
What essential loads are small enough to move by gasoline pickup/van or EV even if semitrailer economics fail?
Can a nearby short line, transload site, river terminal, cooperative, school district, postal route, utility, food bank or farm network become an overflow node?
What return loads can make emergency routes reciprocal rather than one-way?
Which farms are financially vulnerable to diesel and input shocks even if physical production remains possible?
When land changes hands after distress, is ownership/operating control becoming more concentrated, locally distributed, cooperative, public, or otherwise structurally different?

birth_policy.child_scope: one bounded corridor, county, tribal area, island, remote town cluster, commodity shed, or logistics node
triggers: critical service has no credible low-diesel substitute
multiple essential flows share one vulnerable road/terminal/fuel source
local workaround could materially improve resilience
financial distress may cause structural ownership change
pandemic lens changes the priority or viability of the route
local direct reporting conflicts with aggregate data

cross_national_growth.after_us_children_demonstrate_schema: propose analogous national or subnational scouts in other countries
cross_national_growth.continental_threshold: after several validated local/national children exist on a continent, propose a continental synthesis worker
cross_national_growth.global_threshold: after several continental syntheses exist, they may jointly propose a global logistics coordinator
